strengths: The paper presents a technically coherent Algorithms/General contribution: compact multi-layer patch semantics, a global token, and VAE latents are jointly modeled within one SiT backbone, with a complementary representation-alignment objective.

The empirical improvements are substantial. On SiT-B/2 without CFG, REGLUE improves FID from 33.0 for SiT, 24.4 for REPA, 21.4 for ReDi, and 15.2 for REG to 12.9. Improvements persist for unconditional generation and the larger SiT-XL/2 backbone.

The ablation study is unusually thorough. Table 1 separates local versus global semantics, linear versus nonlinear compression, multi-layer aggregation, and external alignment; additional experiments examine bottleneck width, compressor capacity and objectives, VFM choice, CFG settings, and limited-data training.

Matched-channel semantic probing and Cityscapes segmentation results support the proposed explanation that nonlinear compression preserves substantially more useful spatial information than PCA, rather than merely showing an unexplained downstream FID gain.
The method improves convergence meaningfully: SiT-XL/2+REGLUE reaches 4.6 FID at 200K steps and 2.7 at 700K, compared with REG's 5.0 and 2.7 at 200K and 1M steps, respectively.

The manuscript is clear, well organized, and supplies useful architectural and optimization details. The compressor is inexpensive to pretrain, and generation does not require running the VFM or semantic decoder.
weaknesses: The conceptual novelty is moderate. REGLUE primarily combines established ingredients from ReDi, REG, and REPA while replacing PCA with a shallow convolutional autoencoder. The strong empirical result supports publication, but the work is more an effective design refinement and synthesis than a fundamentally new generative formulation.

Evaluation is confined to ImageNet at 256x256. There is no higher-resolution, text-conditioned, or out-of-domain generation experiment, so the generality of the claimed framework beyond this controlled class-conditional benchmark remains uncertain.

No repeated runs, confidence intervals, or statistical uncertainty are reported. This particularly weakens conclusions based on small differences, such as 14.3 versus 14.1 FID for alignment, 13.3 versus 12.9 for the complete configuration, and 2.7 versus 2.5 at large scale.

Efficiency accounting is incomplete. Parameter tables largely exclude the 16.6M-parameter offline compressor and do not report end-to-end training throughput, memory, feature-extraction/precomputation cost, or storage. Thus, claims of lightweight operation and faster training are supported mainly by iteration counts rather than total compute.

Some baseline comparisons are imperfectly normalized: the plain SiT entry uses a 7M-step result while representation-assisted methods use at most 1M steps, and Table 4 mixes training schedules from different methods. The direct REGLUE-versus-REG comparisons are more convincing than the broad state-of-the-art comparison.

Reproducibility is weakened by the blank code URL and several underspecified details, including the exact data split used to train the semantic compressor, class-conditioning/dropout settings, and complete attentive-probe training protocol. The paper also does not examine whether compressor reconstruction quality predicts generation quality across runs or architectures.

strengths: Assessed as Algorithms/General because no contribution type is declared. The paper presents a coherent extension of SiT that jointly models VAE latents, compressed spatial VFM features, and a global VFM token, with an auxiliary representation-alignment loss.

The central empirical result is meaningful: on ImageNet 256×256 without CFG, REGLUE improves SiT-B/2 from 33.0 to 12.9 FID and outperforms matched REPA, ReDi, and REG baselines; improvements also persist with SiT-XL/2 and in unconditional generation.

The ablation study is unusually extensive. Table 1 separates local and global modeling, linear versus nonlinear compression, multi-layer features, and external alignment. Additional experiments examine bottleneck dimensionality, compressor capacity, VFM layers, alternative compressor losses, different VFMs, limited-data training, and CFG settings.

The nonlinear compressor is supported by downstream semantic probes: at matched eight-channel dimensionality it retains substantially more classification and segmentation information than PCA while producing better generative FID.

The method adds little sampling-time overhead because the semantic compressor and VFM are unnecessary during generation, while the diffusion-backbone sequence grows by only one global token. The manuscript is generally clear and includes useful architectural and optimization details.
Results include FID, sFID, Inception Score, precision, and recall, as well as visually strong uncurated class-conditional samples.
weaknesses: The conceptual novelty is modest. REGLUE largely combines ideas already present in REPA, ReDi, and REG, replacing PCA with a small convolutional autoencoder and aggregating several VFM layers. The paper does not provide a deeper theoretical or mechanistic explanation for why reconstruction MSE compression is particularly suitable for diffusion.

Evidence is confined almost entirely to ImageNet at 256×256 with one diffusion family. There is no evaluation at higher resolution, on a second generation dataset, with text conditioning, or with another generator architecture, so the breadth of the claimed unified framework is not established.

The strongest SiT-XL/2 gains over REG at matched training budgets are small—4.6 versus 5.0, 3.2 versus 3.4, and 2.5 versus 2.7 FID—and no repeated runs, uncertainty estimates, or significance analysis are provided. This makes the robustness of the headline advantage unclear.

Training efficiency is reported primarily in iterations or epochs rather than total FLOPs, wall-clock time, storage, or end-to-end accelerator hours. The comparison omits VFM feature extraction and compressor training, and the parameter tables exclude the 16.6M-parameter compressor. Consequently, claims of substantially faster or essentially unchanged training cost are not fully supported.

The nonlinear-versus-linear comparison is not uniformly controlled. Some headline comparisons conflate compression type, bottleneck width, and single- versus multi-layer inputs. The matched eight-channel PCA comparison helps, but its exact probing protocol and diffusion results are mainly conveyed through plots rather than a complete controlled table.

Important reproducibility details remain missing or unclear: the dataset and preprocessing used to train the compressor are not explicitly identified, class-conditioning and CFG dropout are absent from the mathematical description, seeds are not reported, and the stated code link is blank.

The compressor design is selected through many ImageNet-FID ablations on the same benchmark used for final reporting, raising possible benchmark overfitting. Validation on another dataset would be more persuasive.

The qualitative evidence lacks nearest-neighbor or memorization analysis, which would be valuable given the highly photographic ImageNet samples and the use of a large pretrained VFM. Societal impacts and dependencies inherited from the VFM and ImageNet are also not discussed.

Overall, the empirical gains narrowly support acceptance, but the incremental contribution, limited evaluation breadth, absent variance estimates, and incomplete end-to-end efficiency accounting keep the recommendation borderline rather than strong.

strengths: The paper presents a technically coherent Algorithms/General contribution that unifies three previously separate ideas: joint diffusion over VAE latents and spatial VFM features, global-token modeling, and external representation alignment. Channel-wise fusion preserves the SiT token count, making the design practically attractive.

The empirical gains are strong, especially for local nonlinear semantic modeling. On SiT-B/2 without CFG, REGLUE improves FID from 33.0 for SiT and 15.2 for REG to 12.9. The gains persist with SiT-XL/2, where REGLUE reaches 4.6, 3.2, and 2.5 FID at 200K, 400K, and 1M iterations, respectively, consistently improving on the reported REG results.

The ablation suite is unusually extensive and supports the main qualitative conclusions. Table 1 separates local versus global signals, linear versus nonlinear compression, multi-layer aggregation, and alignment; additional experiments examine compressor width, bottleneck size, layer selection, objectives, VFM choice, CFG, unconditional generation, and limited-data training.

The semantic-preservation probes on ImageNet classification and Cityscapes segmentation provide evidence beyond FID that the learned compressor retains useful spatial information. The large improvement over PCA is plausible and relevant to the proposed mechanism.

The method incurs only a small increase in diffusion-model parameters (e.g., 675M to 677M for SiT-XL/2), and the generated samples exhibit good fidelity and diversity. The paper is generally clear, well organized, and sufficiently detailed about the core architecture and optimization settings.
weaknesses: The conceptual novelty is moderate: the primary advance is a learned convolutional replacement for ReDi's PCA, followed by a combination of already established REPA, REG, and multi-layer-feature components. The strong empirical execution makes this valuable, but the framing sometimes overstates the novelty of the overall joint-modeling framework.

There is an important inconsistency or confound in the compressor analysis. The appendix associates the 8-channel nonlinear representation with 14.3 FID and the 16-channel representation with 13.3 FID, whereas Figure 5 and Table 6 indicate that a 16-channel last-layer representation obtains 14.3 and that 13.3 results from using the last four layers. Thus the probing plots appear to change both bottleneck dimensionality and input layers, weakening the claim that their trend isolates compression dimensionality. This should be clarified and corrected.

No repeated runs, uncertainty estimates, or significance analysis are reported. This matters particularly for the comparatively small SiT-XL/2 improvements over REG, such as 4.6 versus 5.0, 3.2 versus 3.4, and 2.5 versus 2.7 FID. The much larger SiT-B/2 improvements are nevertheless convincing.

The efficiency discussion focuses on diffusion parameters and training iterations but does not provide end-to-end training cost, memory, sampling throughput, or preprocessing/storage costs relative to REG and ReDi. Extracting four VFM layers and training the compressor adds overhead, so claims of essentially unchanged compute are only partially substantiated.

Evaluation is restricted to ImageNet at 256x256 and the SiT family. Results at higher resolution or on another dataset would better establish generality, although the consistent B/2 and XL/2 results already provide meaningful evidence.
The manuscript states that code is available, but the link is blank in the submitted PDF. Some reproducibility details are also missing, including random seeds and the gradient-clipping threshold.

strengths: Under the default Algorithms/General category, the paper presents a technically coherent extension of SiT that jointly diffuses VAE latents, compressed spatial VFM features, and a global token, complemented by representation alignment.

The central empirical gains are substantial: on SiT-B/2 at 400K steps, REGLUE improves FID from 33.0 for SiT, 24.4 for REPA, 21.4 for ReDi, and 15.2 for REG to 12.9. Improvements also persist at SiT-XL/2 scale and in unconditional generation.

The unusually thorough component ablation distinguishes local versus global semantics, linear versus nonlinear compression, multilayer aggregation, external alignment, compression width/capacity, VFM choice, fusion strategy, and resampling method. In particular, nonlinear local modeling alone reaches 14.3 FID versus 21.4 for the PCA-based alternative.

The paper supports its FID results with sFID, precision/recall, Inception Score, CMMD, FD/FD-infinity, ImageNet probing, and Cityscapes segmentation. Compute-matched comparisons indicate that the gains are not simply caused by greater training cost.

Evidence extends beyond the principal ImageNet-256 setting to unconditional generation, limited-data training, Food-101, ImageNet-512, multiple VFMs, two SiT scales, and visually convincing class-conditional samples.
The method and compressor are described clearly, and the supplement provides architectures, optimization settings, sampling details, compute estimates, and a candid discussion of scaling limitations.
weaknesses: The conceptual novelty is moderate: the framework largely combines the established ingredients of ReDi-style joint local-feature diffusion, REG-style global-token modeling, and REPA alignment. The main new ingredient is replacing PCA with a learned convolutional autoencoder and aggregating multiple VFM layers; this is effective but relatively incremental.

No results include multiple random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance analysis. This matters particularly for small claimed gains such as 2.7 to 2.5 FID at XL scale, 14.3 to 14.1 from external alignment, and 12.9 to 12.3 from DINOv3.

The nonlinear-versus-PCA comparison does not fully disentangle nonlinearity from learned compressor capacity, architecture, optimization, and feature dimensionality. Comparisons against stronger learned linear compressors or equally trained alternative bottlenecks would better support the claim that nonlinearity itself is decisive.

Claims of essentially unchanged inference cost are slightly overstated: parameters rise from 130M to 132M and measured throughput falls from 4.1 to 3.8 images/s. Training additionally requires VFM extraction and offline compressor training, even though the supplied PFLOP accounting suggests this overhead is small.

Generalization evidence remains limited. Food-101 and ImageNet-512 are reported only through single FID entries with sparse setup details, while the comprehensive study remains centered on ImageNet and DINO-family representations; CLIP-L performs considerably worse.

Reproducibility is weakened by the absence of repeated-run statistics and by the abstract ending with “The code is available at” without an actual URL. Some implementation details are inherited from prior work rather than fully enumerated.

Several presentation issues should be corrected: the prose after Eq. 4 swaps the meanings of the semantic and CLS prediction heads, some causal interpretations of the frequency analysis are stronger than the correlational evidence, and the qualitative section covers only six selected classes without baseline comparisons.

strengths: As an Algorithms/General submission, the paper presents a technically coherent extension of SiT that jointly models VAE latents, compressed spatial VFM features, and a global VFM token, while retaining the original token-grid size through channel-wise fusion.

The empirical gains are substantial in the main ImageNet setting: at 400K steps, SiT-B/2 improves from 33.0 FID to 12.9, compared with 24.4 for REPA, 21.4 for ReDi, and 15.2 for REG. At XL scale, the method reaches 2.5 FID at 1M steps and matches REG's 1M-step result using 700K steps.

The ablation study is unusually comprehensive. It separates local and global semantics, external alignment, linear versus nonlinear compression, multi-layer features, bottleneck dimensionality, compressor capacity, fusion strategy, VFM choice, and resampling method.

The authors provide useful evidence for the proposed compressor beyond generation FID: probing accuracy, Cityscapes segmentation, reconstruction error, and frequency-profile analyses consistently suggest that nonlinear compression preserves more semantic information than PCA.

Evaluation includes unconditional generation, alternative metrics such as CMMD and FD-infinity, limited-data experiments, Food-101, ImageNet-512, and explicit compute accounting. The supplement supplies most architecture and optimization details needed for reproduction.
weaknesses: The conceptual novelty is limited. The main recipe combines ideas already established by ReDi, REG, and REPA, with the principal new mechanism being replacement of PCA by a small convolutional autoencoder plus multi-layer feature concatenation. The term 'unified framework' somewhat overstates this incremental integration.

The evaluation lacks uncertainty estimates, repeated runs, or significance tests. This is especially important for the smaller headline differences at XL scale, such as 2.7 versus 2.5 FID without guidance and 1.59 versus 1.46 with guidance. It is unclear how much of these gains exceeds run-to-run variance or hyperparameter-selection effects.

The evidence for generality remains narrow: nearly all detailed conclusions are drawn from class-conditional ImageNet with SiT and DINO features. Food-101 and ImageNet-512 receive only one small FID table, with insufficient setup details and no qualitative or multi-metric analysis. There is no evaluation on text-conditioned generation, another diffusion backbone, or a substantially different visual domain.

Efficiency claims need more careful qualification. REGLUE has essentially the same inference throughput as REG, but is slower and larger than vanilla SiT; it also requires VFM extraction and offline compressor training. The compute table is helpful, yet peak memory, end-to-end training throughput, preprocessing/storage costs, and the cost of extensive compressor selection are not reported.

Some empirical presentation issues reduce confidence. Table 12 contains duplicated configurations and suspiciously identical values across distinct guidance scales, the qualitative samples use CFG 4.0 rather than the quantitatively selected 2.3 setting, and the abstract states that code is available without supplying a link. Several strong causal statements, including that high-frequency suppression explains improved 'diffusability,' are supported only by correlation rather than controlled intervention.

Jointly generated semantic variables are discarded by the image decoder. The paper does not analyze whether their sampled values are meaningful, whether semantic-image consistency holds, or whether comparable gains could be obtained with a simpler auxiliary-target formulation that avoids generating unused outputs. This leaves the necessity of the full joint generative interpretation insufficiently established.

strengths: Under the default Algorithms/General category, the paper presents a technically coherent and useful extension of representation-entangled diffusion: compact nonlinear patch semantics, a global token, and external alignment are integrated into one SiT model.

The empirical gains are strong and consistent. On ImageNet-256 without CFG, SiT-XL/2+REGLUE obtains 4.6, 3.2, and 2.5 FID at 200K, 400K, and 1M iterations, respectively, improving over matched REG results of 5.0, 3.4, and 2.7. It also matches REG's 1M-step FID using 700K steps.

The ablation suite is unusually thorough. Table 1 separates local versus global semantics, linear versus nonlinear compression, multi-layer features, and alignment; further experiments examine bottleneck width, compressor capacity, VFM layers, alternative VFMs, fusion strategy, resampling, CFG, and limited-data training.

The learned compressor is supported by more than generation FID: attentive probing, Cityscapes segmentation, reconstruction error, and frequency profiles consistently suggest that it preserves substantially more semantic information than PCA while producing a diffusion-friendly representation.

The authors report compute-matched comparisons, alternative distributional metrics, unconditional generation, Food-101, ImageNet-512, and qualitative samples. These results make a persuasive case that the improvement is not solely an Inception-metric artifact.

The paper is clearly organized, provides detailed architecture and optimization settings, and candidly discusses limitations related to long-schedule and high-resolution scaling. weaknesses: The conceptual novelty is moderate: the principal contribution combines ideas already represented by ReDi, REG, and REPA, with a relatively simple convolutional autoencoder replacing PCA. The value is primarily in the design finding and empirical execution rather than a fundamentally new generative formulation.

No repeated runs, error bars, or seed-sensitivity analysis are reported. This matters particularly for the comparatively small improvements over REG at XL scale—0.2 FID without CFG and 0.13–0.27 FID in the guided comparisons—even though the larger gains over SiT, REPA, and ReDi are convincing.

The evaluation remains heavily ImageNet-centric. Food-101 and ImageNet-512 appear only as a small supplementary table using SiT-B/2; broader domains, open-ended text conditioning, and qualitative high-resolution evidence are absent, limiting confidence in generality.

The manuscript says that code is available but gives no URL. Although many implementation details are supplied, releasing code and specifying seeds, gradient-clipping magnitude, feature-precomputation/storage procedures, and all inherited SiT settings would materially improve reproducibility.

Claims of essentially unchanged inference cost should be phrased more precisely: the method increases SiT-XL/2 from 675M to 677M parameters and the reported base-model throughput decreases from 4.1 to 3.8 images/s. The overhead is small, but not literally absent.

The frequency-profile analysis is suggestive rather than causal; it correlates reduced high-frequency energy with improved diffusion performance but does not isolate whether this property, semantic preservation, or another learned-compression effect produces the gain.
